t: Made sultan at twelve and set aside two years later, Mehmed returned to the throne in 1451 and at twenty-one took Constantinople after a fifty-seven-day siege, ending the Byzantine Empire.

His thirty years of war added Serbia, the Morea, Trebizond, Bosnia, Albania and the Anatolian beyliks to the empire, at the cost of mass captivity, executions and deportations, and he made Istanbul a thriving capital again.

He centralised government under officials of devshirme background, codified law and legalised the killing of a new sultan's brothers, and he is remembered as a hero in Turkey and, in the Christian world of his day, as a bloodthirsty tyrant.
dyk: To get past the boom chain across the Golden Horn in 1453, Mehmed had about eighty galleys carried overland around the Genoese colony of Galata on a road of wood little over a mile long.
ev: Born at Edirne, the son of Sultan Murad II and Hüma Hatun
Made sultan at twelve when Murad II abdicates; Murad returns to command the army and wins at Varna
Takes Constantinople after a fifty-seven-day siege and moves the Ottoman capital there
Fails to take Belgrade from John Hunyadi and is wounded fighting in person
Takes Trebizond, absorbing the last vestige of Byzantine rule after the Morea
Defeats Uzun Hasan of the Aq Qoyunlu at the Battle of Otlukbeli
The Treaty of Constantinople ends the long war with Venice, which cedes Shkodra and Negroponte
Falls ill at Maltepe at the start of a new campaign and dies

f.born: 30 March 1432 at Edirne, then the Ottoman capital; son of Sultan Murad II and of Hüma Hatun, a slave of uncertain origin
f.died: 3 May 1481, aged forty-nine, after falling ill at Maltepe at the start of a new campaign; the historian Colin Heywood sees substantial circumstantial evidence of poisoning, possibly at the behest of his son Bayezid; buried in his türbe near the Fatih Mosque
f.role: Ottoman sultan from August 1444 to September 1446 and from February 1451 to May 1481; governor of Amasya as a boy and of Manisa from 1446 to 1451; after 1453 claimed the title caesar of Rome (Qayser-i Rûm)
f.known: the conquest of Constantinople in 1453; the end of the Byzantine Empire and of its last states in the Morea and Trebizond; the conquests of Serbia, Bosnia and Anatolia's beyliks; rebuilding and repopulating Istanbul; codifying law in the kanunname; legalising royal fratricide; his library and patronage of Italian artists
